papers_read.title_as_printed: 18F-FDG-PET-based deep learning for predicting cognitive decline in non-demented elderly across the Alzheimer's disease clinical spectrum (Sohn et al., Radiology Advances 2024, 1(3), umae021)

FDG-PET brain glucose hypometabolism predicts Alzheimer's disease progression pathways in cognitively normal adults: A longitudinal competing risks modeling (Alhasan et al., Metabolism Open 28 (2025) 100400). The map title reads 'Baseline FDG-PET brain glucose hypometabolism determines ...'; authors, cohort (1136 ADNI CN) and results match the record, so this is taken as the same paper under a variant title.

what_each_reports.P-1153: CNN trained on ADNI AD vs NC FDG-PET (test AUC 0.97; external J-ADNI AUC 0.98) gives an AD-similarity score. Prognosis via Cox models with clinical features + SUVR (Model 1) vs + DL output (Model 2): ADNI MCI (n = 663, MCI to AD over up to 9 years) iAUC 0.768 -> 0.787, difference 0.020 [0.007-0.034]; J-ADNI MCI (n = 129) 0.694 -> 0.716, difference 0.020 [-0.005 to 0.044]; HABS NC (n = 274, NC to MCI) 0.817 -> 0.902, difference 0.059 [-0.003 to 0.126]. DL HR 3.45 / 2.28 / 4.57. Amyloid-positive ADNI MCI 4-year tdAUC 0.720 -> 0.739.
what_each_reports.P-1154: 1136 cognitively normal ADNI participants; four post-defined pathways (stable 32.8%, CN->MCI only 34.9%, CN->MCI->AD 15.8%, CN->AD direct 16.5%). Multinomial logistic regression with FDG MetaROI z-score as primary predictor 'supplemented by baseline cognitive measures when appropriate'; temporal and subject-grouped cross-validation within ADNI. Direct AD conversion AUC 0.999 (12 m), 0.994 (24 m), 0.994 (36 m); MCI as first event AUC 0.686 / 0.643 / 0.680. Direct conversion 17.12 vs 2.31 per 100 person-years (low vs high FDG), 7.4-fold.

quantity_a: Incremental prognostic value (difference in integrated time-dependent AUC from Cox models) of adding a CNN FDG-PET score to clinical features and SUVR, for MCI-to-AD conversion in baseline-MCI cohorts (ADNI, J-ADNI) and NC-to-MCI conversion in HABS NC.
quantity_b: Absolute fixed-horizon ROC-AUC of a multinomial model (FDG MetaROI z-score plus baseline cognition) for membership in a 'direct CN-to-AD without documented MCI' pathway, and for MCI as first event, in ADNI cognitively normal participants.
incompatible_if_same: The apparent gap (0.787 vs 0.994) compares an incremental-model iAUC in MCI with an absolute pathway-classification AUC in CN; if one forced the nearest analogue (CN cohorts predicting NC->MCI), P-1153 HABS gives iAUC 0.817-0.902 with PACC-based clinical features plus SUVR/DL while P-1154 gives AUC 0.64-0.69 for MCI as first event, but predictor sets, cohorts (HABS vs ADNI), event definitions and metric construction all differ, so no incompatibility on one estimand can be established.

gates.dataset_family: partial: P-1154 is ADNI only; P-1153's ADNI stratum is MCI (not CN) and its CN stratum is HABS, so no shared population stratum exists.
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-1153 tests across three cohorts (J-ADNI, HABS beyond ADNI); P-1154 is internal cross-validation within ADNI only. No waiver on record.
gates.modality_family: match at family level (FDG-PET); representation differs (CNN AD-similarity score added to SUVR vs single MetaROI z-score).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: endpoints differ (MCI-to-AD conversion or NC-to-MCI vs direct CN-to-AD bypass pathway); metric types differ (iAUC from Cox and its increment over a clinical model vs fixed-horizon ROC-AUC of a multinomial classifier); baseline populations differ (MCI vs CN).
performance_validity: flag applies to P-1154 in substance: AUC 0.994-0.999 on internal ADNI cross-validation with no external cohort; the sample is not small (1136), but the near-ceiling figure is internal only and the paper's own internals are inconsistent (a 'cognitively normal' cohort containing an 'MCI at baseline (MMSE 20-23)' stratum; 16.5% direct CN-to-dementia conversion). P-1153's AD vs NC AUC 0.97/0.98 is a diagnostic-classification figure with an external J-ADNI test and is not the contested quantity.
independence: Both draw on ADNI (P-1153 ADNI MCI; P-1154 ADNI CN) but on disjoint baseline strata; distinct author teams.
grounds: P-1153 reports how much a deep-learning FDG score adds to a clinical-plus-SUVR Cox model (iAUC difference 0.020 in ADNI MCI), whereas P-1154 reports the absolute AUC of a multinomial pathway classifier; an increment and an absolute AUC are different metric types.
The endpoints differ: MCI-to-AD conversion (ADNI/J-ADNI MCI) or NC-to-MCI (HABS) in P-1153, versus direct CN-to-AD conversion without documented MCI in P-1154.
The baseline populations differ: P-1153's ADNI and J-ADNI strata are MCI at baseline; P-1154 contains only ADNI participants labelled cognitively normal.
P-1154's 0.994 is internal ADNI cross-validation only and near ceiling, so it cannot anchor a cross-study performance comparison under Section 2 in any case.

evidence_quotes.quote: The addition of DL output to clinical features and SUVR significantly improved the prognosis prediction in the ADNI MCI set (iAUC 0.768 [0.744-0.791] and 0.787 [0.766-0.811] for Model 1 and 2, respectively, iAUC difference 0.020 [0.007-0.034])
the main outcome was conversion from MCI to AD-dementia in the ADNI MCI and J-ADNI MCI sets, and from NC to MCI in the HABS NC set.
HABS NC Clinical features þ SUVR 0.817 (0.692-0.909) NA Clinical features þ SUVR þ DL 0.902 (0.751-0.951) 0.059 (−0.003 to 0.126)
We analyzed 1136 cognitively normal participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative with baseline fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)
Pathway prediction modeling utilized multinomial logistic regression with brain glucose metabolism as the primary predictor, supplemented by baseline cognitive measures when appropriate.
Direct Alzheimer's disease conversion prediction achieved high accuracy across time horizons: 12-month AUC of 0.999, 24-month AUC of 0.994, and 36-month AUC of 0.994
Among participants with MCI at baseline (MMSE 20–23), low FDG metabolism resulted in six-fold higher risk

record_defects: conflict_statement says P-1154's AUC 0.994 comes 'from a baseline FDG MetaROI z-score'; the Methods state the multinomial model was 'supplemented by baseline cognitive measures when appropriate', so it is not a standalone FDG figure.
claim_a labels P-1153 V3; the registry row says V4. The PDF shows external testing in J-ADNI and HABS; the tier label is inconsistent between record and registry.
The record and map quote P-1154's title with 'determines'; the printed title uses 'predicts' (the abstract does say hypometabolism 'determined pathway selection').

The record describes P-1154 labels as 'constructed post hoc'; the PDF defines the four pathways from longitudinal diagnoses as outcomes, which is standard; the substantive issue is internal-only validation and internal inconsistencies (an 'MCI at baseline' stratum inside a CN cohort), which the record does not mention.
residual_risk and gate note say the pair 'passes all four deterministic gates'; the validation-tier gate does not match on the PDFs (multi-cohort testing vs internal ADNI cross-validation).
what_would_change_the_verdict: A study reporting an externally validated absolute AUC for FDG-PET prediction of the same endpoint (e.g. CN-to-AD within a fixed horizon, same predictor set) whose interval excludes P-1154's value; the two documents here do not share an estimand.
